message.content:
### Killing **VS Code** (`code.exe`) from the command line | Tool | Command | Notes | |------|---------|-------| | **Command Prompt (cmd.exe)** | `taskkill /IM code.exe /F` | `/IM` – image name (process name).
`/F` – force terminate. | | **PowerShell** | `Stop-Process -Name code -Force` | Equivalent to the above. | | **Task Manager** | Right‑click → **End task** | GUI method. | --- #### 1. Using `taskkill` (Command Prompt) ```cmd taskkill /IM code.exe /F ``` - **`/IM code.exe`** tells Windows to look for any process whose executable name is `code.exe`. - **`/F`** forces the termination (useful if the process is hung). - If you want to also kill child processes spawned by VS Code, add `/T`: ```cmd taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T ``` > **Tip:** If you’re running this from a script and want to suppress the “process not found” error, redirect stderr to nul: ```cmd taskkill /IM code.exe /F 2>nul ``` --- #### 2. Using PowerShell ```powershell Stop-Process -Name code -Force ``` - `-Name code` matches the process name (`code.exe`). - `-Force` forces termination. If you prefer the same syntax as `taskkill`: ```powershell Stop-Process -Name code -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue ``` --- #### 3. From within VS Code (Developer Tools) If you just want to restart VS Code without killing all background processes: 1. Press `Ctrl+Shift+P` (or `Cmd+Shift+P` on macOS). 2. Type **Developer: Reload Window** and hit Enter. This reloads the window but keeps the underlying `code.exe` process alive. --- #### 4. Common pitfalls | Issue | Fix | |-------|-----| | “Access is denied” | Run the command prompt or PowerShell **as Administrator**. | | “The process cannot be terminated” | Use `/F` (force) or `/T` (terminate child processes). | | “No instance found” | Make sure VS Code is actually running; check the Task Manager. | --- #### 5. Quick one‑liner for batch scripts ```cmd @echo off taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T 2>nul ``` This silently kills VS Code if it’s running, otherwise does nothing. --- ### Summary - **Command Prompt:** `taskkill /IM code.exe /F` - **PowerShell:** `Stop-Process -Name code -Force` - **GUI:** End task in Task Manager. Use the one that best fits your workflow. Happy coding!
